title: Portal, HotSpot and RADIUS: three jobs
fact: The captive portal is the guest webpage. MikroTik HotSpot controls network access. RADIUS checks credentials, supplies access rules and receives usage reports.
why: Payment approval creates a stored access entitlement; the network adapter still needs to provision credentials and enforcement before a guest can use it.
requirements: HotSpot can use local accounts without RADIUS. Cloud RADIUS or local User Manager are authentication choices; their adapters are not connected in this build.

title: Your router may host a RADIUS server
fact: MikroTik User Manager is a separate RADIUS server package. The documented active-session limits are Level 4: 20, Level 5: 50 and Level 6: unlimited by license.
why: At approximately 50 guests, a Level 4 router cannot host all those User Manager sessions. Multiple connections from one guest count as separate sessions.
requirements: Check exact model, RouterOS version, architecture, storage and license. User Manager excludes SMIPS. Unlimited licensing does not guarantee hardware capacity. Local integration is proposed, not implemented.

title: WireGuard connects your router to Magic Hub
fact: WireGuard creates an encrypted tunnel and authenticates peers using keys. Guest voucher authentication is a separate HotSpot/RADIUS operation.
why: Our proposed configuration uses the tunnel for router management and cloud RADIUS traffic, while guest internet stays on the site WAN or Starlink.
requirements: Requires supported RouterOS, configured keys, routes and firewall isolation. A registered router or exported onboarding plan does not prove a live tunnel or connectivity.
